claims.text: The magnetocaloric response of as-deposited Fe25Ni21Mn24Si13Ge17 films and nanoribbons is primarily governed by localized short-range atomic order and residual internal strain.
The hysteresis of as-deposited Fe25Ni21Mn24Si13Ge17 films and nanoribbons is primarily governed by localized short-range atomic order and residual internal strain.
The as-deposited material is amorphous or extremely fine and disordered.
The as-deposited material has a single cubic-type short-range order.
Annealing at 700 K relieves fabrication-induced internal strain.
Annealing at 700 K induces subtle short-range atomic reordering without bulk crystallization.
Strain relaxation and short-range atomic reordering reduce local domain-pinning barriers.
Strain relaxation and short-range atomic reordering enhance collective exchange interactions.
Reduced pinning and enhanced exchange increase the effective ferromagnetic volume.
Annealing at 700 K should increase maximum magnetization relative to the as-deposited baseline.
Annealing at 700 K should increase the magnitude of the conventional isothermal magnetic entropy change relative to the as-deposited baseline.
Annealing at 700 K should reduce hysteretic losses relative to the as-deposited baseline.
The as-deposited 1 µm-spaced nanoribbon baseline has a peak −ΔSM of approximately 1.25 J kg−1 K−1 at 140 K under a 50 kOe field change.
Elastic longitudinal strain up to 2% should stabilize magnetic order, especially above 100 K.
Elastic longitudinal strain up to 2% should not shift the blocking peak.
A broad conventional magnetocaloric response occurs over approximately 40–200 K.
Below approximately 20 K, edge-related spin frustration may dominate the magnetic behavior.
Annealing at 700 K lies within the metastable pre-crystallization regime for this material.

contradictions.description: The explanation is framed around low-applied-field cooling cycles, but the only quantified entropy-change baseline and the proposed entropy measurements use a field change up to 50 kOe, which is not clearly a low-field condition.

The hypothesis is explicitly restricted to a pre-crystallization regime, yet detectable bulk crystallization is designated as falsification. Crystallization would instead show that the intervention left the stated applicability boundary and would not by itself refute the proposed mechanism within that boundary.
